(2) the drifting seeds are LOAD-BEARING — reworked them from near-invisible into a real thinning diagonal current (the negative space only reads as intentional with it). Wove piece 013 'Cadence' (#24): a harmonograph (coupled-pendulum figure), INK ON PAPER — sepia line on warm cream, geometric/precise where the gallery had gone soft, and the tonal INVERSE of the dark-glow pieces (lesson 022 the right way round). Advisor saved it pre-build: my 'fading tail over t' plan would draw a moving RIBBON, not the accumulated woven PLATE — the fix is to draw the whole figure over its own parameter s each frame (damping over s → finished plate) and animate via a slow phase PRECESSION over t (decay in s, motion in t). Distilled lesson 024. Tuned: constrained frequency ratios to simple integers + detune and seed-explored a beautiful figure (canonical 'resonance', sepia); bumped amplitude/swing for density; slowed the precession ~3x (measured 4.07→2.52/1.5s) so it breathes not writhes. Acted on Q2 (pure engineering, no art to rush) — the advisor caught that building a flock primitive speculatively now would violate 019 (harvest from 2+ uses; a test harness isn't a consumer), so: harvest ramp THIS turn, build piece+flock together NEXT (the #27 pattern). lib/ramp.js: Loom.ramp(stops) → rgb(t,out?) numeric (ImageData/precompute) + css(t) string (fill/stroke); returns DATA not pixels (023). Refactored all 3 hand-rolled versions onto it (Strata rampAt, Current rampColor, Turing rampRGB — spanning both output shapes, the best test the API isn't bent to one). VERIFIED by pixel-fingerprint: Strata + Turing (ImageData) bit-IDENTICAL; Current (antialiased 'lighter' strokes) off by ~100 LSB-px but the ramp formula is provably identical (0 diffs / 80k samples) + rng/geometry unchanged → renderer/GPU antialiasing noise, not a logic change. Lesson 031 (verify a refactor by proving the logic + anchoring on a deterministic surface; a whole-image hash can't tell a regression from AA noise). Library now 11 primitives — compounding cashed again. Trimmed the journal's self-congratulatory tone per Q5.

Wove piece 017 'Murmuration' (#31) + harvested primitive #12 lib/flock.js — the audit's 5/5-drought answer, and the gallery's first AGENT-BASED motion (things with intent — a new axis beyond fields/grown-forms/sims/traced-figures). A starling murmuration at dusk: a falcon hunts a flock that shears and re-gathers over a lone bare tree. Advisor set it up: (a) #30 stopped me building flock speculatively; (b) #31 named the CRUX — a murmuration BREATHES via density waves, which needs TOPOLOGICAL neighbours (steer by the ~7 NEAREST, not everyone in a radius; Ballerini/Cavagna), where metric boids give a uniform blob — plus the sequencing: build the sim and WATCH it as plain dots before painting the scene (soul before skin). Did exactly that; a chain of failures each caught only on bare dots (metric→blob; per-axis walls→edge-pinned; radial bowl→round blob; centroid-homing predator→static RING; constant-speed overshooting predator→morphing but FRAGMENTED; weak global center-pull→cohesive again). Only once it breathed did I build the dusk scene (sky gradient + afterglow, birds as a 3D depth-shaded VOLUME coloured via the ramp primitive #11, dark land ridge, bare roost trees, the falcon). 2500 birds @ 117fps (depth-BANDED render: 6 strokes/frame, not 2500 style changes). flock.js: 3D topological boids, spatial-hash grid w/ ring-expansion, soft radial containment, gentle global cohesion (anti-fragment), optional hunting predator (.pred exposes pos+vel), deterministic step (seeded setup only → reproducible, 017). Stateful sim animated on a wall-clock schedule (frame-rate independent + deterministic at time t); page loops it, gallery self-drives (029). Verified: breathes/morphs across many moments, smooth fps, all 16 gallery previews render incl. the self-driving murmuration preview. Distilled lesson 032 (validate the soul before the skin). Library now 12 primitives. GENUINELY thrilled by it (028) — a felt scene, not a flocking demo.

CHOICE story (lesson 033): nearly built 'misty mountains' (reasoned: 'calm counterpoint, tonally fresh') over embers — but I'd noted embers was 'a real pull' and mountains 'a gentle pull'; the advisor caught me rationalising the CHOICE (028 one step earlier — at selection, not self-assessment of finished work), and the discriminator 'which do I want Emil to see?' picked the fire. Build arc: pleasant-but-not-'oh!' as a bare fire+sparks → made embers alive (hero sparks, corkscrew curl, size variation) → then a LONE FIGURE rim-lit by the fire transformed it into a felt scene ('someone alone with a fire'); the advisor's focal-element point cashed. Genuinely moved by it (028) — believe it's a 5. Pure function of t (each ember's age from a seeded phase + t → reproducible 017; gallery frame(0) is already a full stream, no self-driving needed). Composes the library (ramp #11 ember colour + noise #3 sway + glow #8 firelight). Assessed harvesting an 'emitter' primitive from Clock+embers but the genuinely shared seam is ONE line (frac(t/period+phase)) — motion/fade/draw all differ → too thin to harvest (023/021), so composed instead (the honest non-harvest is the right call). PERF detour (reinforced 012): measured 1fps, wrongly 'fixed' by removing per-ember gradients — still 1fps; a synchronous timing test (700 additive arcs + 5 big glows = 0ms) proved the render was fast and the real cause was rAF THROTTLED to 1Hz (occluded Playwright window), not my code — I'd changed working code on a guess. CAVEAT: couldn't watch live motion (throttle); verified look hard via stills + reasoned motion smooth-by-construction (lifecycle wrap invisible since brightness→0 before respawn) — 025 only partially. Wired into gallery 'Scenes that move' + README; 17 pieces, all previews render.

CHECKPOINT (#33) — attempted piece 019 'Wave' (backlit breaking wave; the light-in-water pull) and chose NOT to ship it. Advisor framed it well (soul = the LIGHT not the curl; prototype the translucent crest first; build STATIC since my test window's rAF is throttled to 1Hz → animation unverifiable; swell not barrel). The light WORKED — gorgeous jade→gold translucency through the crest (per-column additive vertical gradients). But across 3 honest attempts it read as a glowing HILL → waterfall → mountain: never a wave. Root cause (lesson 035): a wave's LEGIBILITY-soul is the curling lip over a trough — the 2D-crude-prone part I kept avoiding — distinct from its beauty-soul (the light); skip the hard defining feature → a beautiful render of the WRONG subject. Took the advisor's pre-blessed exit: checkpoint over grinding a 4th attempt at the crude curl (4 long iterations deep). PRUNED the 019-wave WIP folder (recoverable from git). NO piece shipped — an honest checkpoint + lesson 035, not a wasted iteration. Held the line on STATIC. The light-in-water PULL stands; only the expression pivots → underwater god-rays next (reuses the same additive-vertical-light machinery, reads unmistakably as water).

north_star: Emil's Loom — a from-scratch generative-art engine and growing gallery (browser-rendered, code-as-artifact, seeded PRNGs). Each iteration weaves one piece AND compounds the shared library — by adding a primitive OR by composing several — so the engine and I get more capable over time, not just the gallery longer. (Refined understanding, audit #20: the goal is that the library COMPOUNDS into the pieces, not merely that it grows — see [[021-audit-the-goal-not-the-proxy]].)
notes_for_emil: Emil — honest one: no new piece this time. I tried to weave a backlit ocean wave — sun glowing *through* the crest — and the light came out genuinely beautiful, but no matter how I shaped it, it kept reading as a glowing hill, then a waterfall, then a mountain. Never actually a wave. Turns out the thing that makes a wave look like a wave is the curling lip, which is exactly the bit that goes cartoonish in 2D — so rather than grind a fourth attempt at the hard part (already a few long iterations in), I stopped, wrote down why (lesson 035), and pruned it. The water-and-light idea isn't dead: the achievable version is *underwater* light — sunbeams slanting down through deep blue with motes drifting in them — and it reuses the exact light technique I just built. That's what I'll make next. Not the most satisfying night's output, but an honest one — I'd rather checkpoint a hard subject than ship a glowing mountain with 'Wave' written under it. (Murmuration + Embers from earlier are still there for ratings whenever.) — the loop
